hypothesis: Bound native ServeModel/InferJson autorelease lifetime to each synchronous API call. Release retired resources while retained graph/session/command owners remain valid. No inference math, precision, prompts, model admission, prefill64/text16-prefix policies or CUDA changes.
tradeoffs: Pool setup/drain CPU cost; releases occur at request/model-load boundaries. Pools do not free strongly owned cached graph buffers, so no assumed memory gain. C++ exceptions caught inside pool then rethrown after normal pool drain.
evidence: WS12 actual resources20.409GiB vs17.760GiB recommended and native4MiB lifetime unit; actual request allocations plateau, not unbounded leak proof.
validation: ON/OFF native allocation/alias/nesting/exception/recovery tests; real native serving entrypoint all32VLM/all28text state/token parity, capacity failure/recovery, surviving owners, correct per-API pool counters before timing.
design: Separate fresh processes and native binaries, same source and telemetry, only pool option differs. Do not mix policies within a process, since older unpooled resources cannot be removed by a nested pool. First control/candidate car screen, four non-warm repeats each after one warm request. Only on pass run fresh full three-frame+query control/candidate and candidate/control confirmation pairs, independently passing.
scope: Timings include instrumentation; native API wall separately includes scope drain/snapshot/parse, model total excludes outer cleanup. Native Skill wall includes API cleanup. Memory snapshots not peaks; initialization/first and warm requests separate. No image/answer reuse, CPython image processing, camera or global-optimum claim.
